```{r}
# before we merge lets extract taxonomic info into seperate columns
updated_tax_tbl <- contig_tax_otutbl

# Remove '-_cellular organisms;'
updated_tax_tbl$full_tax_id <- gsub("-_cellular organisms;", "", updated_tax_tbl$full_tax_id)


# Remove 'unclassified' labels, supergroups, and prefixes like 'd_', 'p_', etc.
updated_tax_tbl$full_tax_id <- gsub(";?-_[^;]*", "", updated_tax_tbl$full_tax_id)

updated_tax_tbl$full_tax_id <- gsub("(-_unclassified [^;]+;)|(-_pvc [^;]+;)|[dpcosfg]_", "", updated_tax_tbl$full_tax_id)


# Split 'full_tax_id' into separate columns
updated_tax_tbl <- separate(updated_tax_tbl, full_tax_id,
                            into = c("Domain", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species"),
                            sep = ";", fill = "right", extra = "merge")
```

### Phyloseq Analysis of RPS3 centroids (SGs)
#### Setup phy objects (and filtering)
##### Filtering to remove rare taxa

Ulas recommended we filter the data (maybe by count, or mean coverage) to remove rarer taxa so they don't skew the deseq results.
```{r}
# First, try filtering the low abundance taxa in mean. filter out taxa with  >6 samples with a coverage value of 0.10 or less.
# This roughly translates to if 11% or more of the samples have less than 10% coverage, chuck the taxa.
View(contig_tax_mean_merged)
length(contig_tax_mean_merged$OTU) #3198 total taxa

binarize <- function(data, threshold) {
  # Binarize data based on the threshold
  # Values greater than the threshold are set to 1, others to 0
  binary_data <- ifelse(data > threshold, 1, 0)
  return(binary_data)
}
# Filtering at 0.1 reads for > 6 samples only retains 72.7% data
#Try at 0.01 so at least 1% coverage in more than 6% of samples
tb1 <- contig_tax_mean_merged[, 14:77]
tb1 = tb1 %>% as.matrix()
rownames(tb1) = contig_tax_mean_merged[,"full_gene_ID"]
rawcov_threshold = 0.01
samplesover_threshold = 4
tb1_matrix_thresholded = binarize(tb1, rawcov_threshold)
rps3_passed <- ""
rps3_passed = rownames(tb1)[which(apply(tb1, 1, sum) > samplesover_threshold)]
length(rps3_passed) #2865, so 89.5%

#This essentially means a shit ton of low abundant taxa. I think Ill use the less stringent one.
```


##### Norm and Hellinger Transform, make phy_objs
```{r}
sample2bp <- read.table("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Microtrait/microtrait/sample2bp.txt", sep = "\t", header = T)
rps3_norm_f <- contig_tax_mean_merged[contig_tax_mean_merged$full_gene_ID %in% rps3_passed, ]
colnames(rps3_norm_f) <- gsub(".Mean", "", colnames(rps3_norm_f))
head(rps3_norm_f)

for (sample_name in colnames(rps3_norm_f)[14:79]) { # Excluding the "Genome" column
  # Fetch the norm_falization bp from sample2bp based on the sample name
  norm_f_factor <- sample2bp$fastq.total[sample2bp$sample == sample_name]
  
  # norm_falize the values in the current column of 'rps3_norm_f_'
  rps3_norm_f[[sample_name]] <- ((rps3_norm_f[[sample_name]] / norm_f_factor)*100000000)
}
head(rps3_norm_f)

write.csv(rps3_norm_f, file = "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/Taxonomy/rps3_norm_filtered_coverage.csv", row.names = F)

rps3_norm_f <- read_csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/Taxonomy/rps3_norm_filtered_coverage.csv")

view(rps3_norm_f)
#Hellinger Transform
rps3_hell_f <- decostand(rps3_norm_f[, 14:79], method = "hellinger")

# Add the non-sample columns back
rps3_hell_f <- cbind(rps3_norm_f[, 1:13], rps3_hell_f)

# View the transformed data
head(rps3_hell_f)
write.csv(rps3_hell_f, file = "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/Taxonomy/rps3_hellinger_filtered.csv", row.names = F)
```

```{r}
subset_data <- function(physeq, location, vegtype) {
```

```{r}
# Function to subset data by location
subset_by_location <- function(physeq, location) {
  sample_df <- data.frame(sample_data(physeq))

# Function to merge samples by Vegtype
merge_by_vegtype <- function(physeq) {
  sample_df <- data.frame(sample_data(physeq))
  # Check for any missing or invalid Vegtype values
  print(sample_df$Vegtype)
  
  # Ensure Vegtype is a factor
  sample_df$Vegtype <- as.factor(sample_df$Vegtype)
  
  # Check for any NAs in Vegtype
  if(any(is.na(sample_df$Vegtype))) {
    stop("Vegtype contains NA values. Please ensure all samples have a valid Vegtype.")
  }
  
  combined_physeq <- merge_samples(physeq, group = sample_df$Vegtype, fun = "mean")
  return(combined_physeq)
}

# Merge samples by Vegtype

Lowerreaches_Combined <- merge_by_vegtype(lowerreaches_physeq)
Upperreaches_Combined <- merge_by_vegtype(upperreaches_physeq)
```

###### Generate plots
```{r}
# Function to convert phyloseq object to long format data frame for ggplot2
convert_phyloseq_to_long <- function(physeq) {
  # Extract the OTU table and convert to data frame
  otu_df <- as.data.frame(otu_table(physeq))
  otu_df$Vegtype <- rownames(otu_df)
  
  # Convert to long format
  otu_long <- otu_df %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -Vegtype, names_to = "OTU", values_to = "Abundance")
  
  # Extract the taxonomy table and convert to data frame
  tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(physeq))
  tax_df$OTU <- rownames(tax_df)
  
  # Merge OTU table with taxonomy table
  merged_df <- left_join(otu_long, tax_df, by = "OTU")
  
  # Replace NA Phylum with "Unknown"
  merged_df$Phylum[is.na(merged_df$Phylum)] <- "Unknown"
  
  return(merged_df)
}

# Function to create plot from a long format data frame
plot_relative_abundance <- function(long_df, title, show_legend = TRUE) {
  # Ensure Phylum is a factor and set levels with "Unknown" last
  phylum_levels <- c("Nitrososphaerota", "Nitrospirota", sort(setdiff(unique(long_df$Phylum), c("Unknown", "Nitrososphaerota", "Nitrospirota"))), "Unknown")
  long_df$Phylum <- factor(long_df$Phylum, levels = phylum_levels)
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- ggplot(long_df, aes(x = Vegtype, y = Abundance, fill = Phylum)) +
    geom_bar(aes(fill = Phylum), stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = phylum_colors) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Vegetation", y = "Relative Abundance (%)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 14),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 18),
          legend.key.width = unit(.5, "cm"),  # Adjust the width of the legend keys
          legend.key.size = unit(0.2, "cm"),  # Adjust the size of the legend keys (optional)
        #legend.key.size = unit(1, 'cm'),          # Increase legend key size
        #legend.key.width = unit(1, 'cm'),         # Increase legend key width
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12),     # Increase legend text size
        legend.title = element_text(size = 16),    # Increase legend title size
        legend.box.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0),  # Reduce the space around the entire legend
          legend.spacing.x = unit(0.05, "cm"),
          legend.position = ifelse(show_legend, "right", "none")
          )
  
  return(p)
}

# Function to extract the legend from a ggplot
extract_legend <- function(plot) {
  g <- ggplotGrob(plot)
  legend <- gtable_filter(g, "guide-box")
  return(legend)
}
```

##### Richness, Eveness Raw count
```{r}
# Load your phyloseq object (assuming it's named 'phy_norm_f')
phy_raw <- readRDS("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/Taxonomy/phyloseq_raw_count_object.rds")

metadata_wgeology_new <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/metadata_wgeology_new.csv")


# Extract the OTU Table and Phylogenetic Tree
otu_data <- otu_table(phy_raw)
phy_tree_obj <- phy_tree(phy_raw)

# Check for zero-length branches
if(any(phy_tree_obj$edge.length == 0)){
    cat("The tree has zero-length branches.\n")
    # Addressing zero-length branches might be necessary
}

# Use this tree for diversity
zero_length_branches <- which(phy_tree_obj$edge.length == 0)
# If there are zero-length branches, set them to a small value (e.g., 1e-10)
if(length(zero_length_branches) > 0) {
    cat("Number of zero-length branches:", length(zero_length_branches), "\n")
    phy_tree_obj$edge.length[zero_length_branches] <- 1e-9
}

# Calculate the diversity metrics
diversity_data <- ""
diversity_data <- estimate_richness(phy_raw, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Chao1"))
diversity_data$sample <- rownames(diversity_data)

# View the results
print(diversity_data)

# Calculate Pielou's evenness
calculate_pielou <- function(shannon, richness) {
  return(shannon / log(richness))
}

diversity_data$Pielou <- calculate_pielou(diversity_data$Shannon, diversity_data$Observed)

# Merge the diversity data with metadata
merged_data <- left_join(diversity_data, metadata_wgeology_new, by = "sample")

# Compute the mean diversity indices by vegetation type
mean_diversity <- merged_data %>%
  group_by(Vegtype) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_vegtype_shannon = mean(Shannon, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_vegtype_Chao1 = mean(Chao1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_vegtype_Pielou = mean(Pielou, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(mean_diversity)
total_vegtype_diversity <- mean_diversity %>%
  summarise(
    mean_shannon = mean(mean_vegtype_shannon, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_chao = mean(mean_vegtype_Chao1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_pielou = mean(mean_vegtype_Pielou, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  
print(total_vegtype_diversity)

#Reorder based on vegtype
diversity_data <- diversity_data %>%
  mutate(VegetationType = str_sub(sample, 3, 3),
         VegetationType = factor(VegetationType, levels = c("c", "a", "m", "s")),
         sample = factor(sample, levels = sample[order(VegetationType, Chao1)])) %>%
  mutate(location = str_sub(sample, 1, 1),
         location = factor(location, levels = c("H", "L", "U")))
```

##### Ordination vectors (envfit)
```{r}
# vegan::envfit fits each variable as a linear gradient across the first two ordination axes.
# Vegtype is 4-level categorical, so each vegtype is fit as its own 0/1 indicator (Aspen, Conifer,
# Meadow, Sagebrush): each arrow points toward that vegtype and is directly comparable to the pH
# arrow. Continuous / 2-level PERMANOVA terms (pH, moisture, ground cover, depth) get arrows too.
# Arrows are scaled by sqrt(r2) (vegan default), then share one multiplier to fit the point cloud.
# Multi-level factors (Vegtype, Location, block) are also fit as whole factors (r2 / p in the
# table, not drawn: 3 + 9 more arrows would bury the plot; colour / shape / labels show them).
envfit_vectors <- function(ord, phy_obj,
                           vars = c("pH", "perc_moist", "GroundCoverPerc", "depth"),
                           veg_levels = c("Aspen", "Conifer", "Meadow", "Sagebrush"),
                           factors = c("Vegtype", "Location", "block"),
                           strata_var = "block", seed = 420) {
  site <- if (inherits(ord, "metaMDS")) scores(ord, display = "sites") else ord$vectors
  site <- site[, 1:2]
  meta <- data.frame(sample_data(phy_obj))[rownames(site), , drop = FALSE]

  env <- meta[, vars, drop = FALSE] %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(as.character(.x))))
  for (v in veg_levels) env[[v]] <- as.numeric(meta$Vegtype == v)
  # drop anything constant in this subset (e.g. depth within a depth subset, Sagebrush in headwaters)
  env <- env[, sapply(env, function(x) var(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0), drop = FALSE]

  # p.value = free permutations; p.value_strat = permutations restricted within block (same r2 and
  # arrow, only the null changes). Samples within a block aren't exchangeable with other blocks.
  strata <- if (!is.null(strata_var) && n_distinct(meta[[strata_var]]) > 1) factor(meta[[strata_var]]) else NULL
  set.seed(seed)
  fit <- envfit(site, env, permutations = 999, na.rm = TRUE)
  set.seed(seed)
  fit_strat <- envfit(site, env, permutations = 999, strata = strata, na.rm = TRUE)
  arr <- scores(fit, display = "vectors")
  mul <- 0.8 * min(max(abs(site[, 1])) / max(abs(arr[, 1])),
                   max(abs(site[, 2])) / max(abs(arr[, 2])))
  unit_arr <- fit$vectors$arrows
  angle_to_pH <- if ("pH" %in% rownames(unit_arr)) {
    acos(pmin(1, pmax(-1, unit_arr %*% unit_arr["pH", ]))) * 180 / pi
  } else NA_real_

  vec <- data.frame(Variable = rownames(arr),
                    type = ifelse(rownames(arr) %in% veg_levels, "Vegtype_indicator", "vector"),
                    x_plot = arr[, 1] * mul,
                    y_plot = arr[, 2] * mul,
                    r2 = fit$vectors$r,
                    p.value = fit$vectors$pvals,
                    p.value_strat = fit_strat$vectors$pvals,
                    angle_to_pH_deg = as.numeric(angle_to_pH))

  factors <- factors[sapply(meta[factors], function(x) length(unique(x)) > 1)]
  if (length(factors) == 0) return(vec)
  set.seed(seed)
  ffit <- envfit(site, meta[, factors, drop = FALSE] %>% mutate(across(everything(), as.factor)),
                 permutations = 999)
  # block-restricted p only for Vegtype: block (and Location, which nests blocks) can't be tested
  # with permutations that never move samples between blocks
  p_strat_fac <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(factors)), factors)
  if ("Vegtype" %in% factors && !is.null(strata)) {
    set.seed(seed)
    p_strat_fac["Vegtype"] <- envfit(site, meta[, "Vegtype", drop = FALSE] %>% mutate(Vegtype = as.factor(Vegtype)),
                                     permutations = 999, strata = strata)$factors$pvals
  }
  fac <- data.frame(Variable = names(ffit$factors$r), type = "factor",
                    x_plot = NA_real_, y_plot = NA_real_,
                    r2 = ffit$factors$r, p.value = ffit$factors$pvals,
                    p.value_strat = unname(p_strat_fac[names(ffit$factors$r)]), angle_to_pH_deg = NA_real_)
  bind_rows(vec, fac)
}

add_envfit_vectors <- function(p, ord, phy_obj, label_size = 3) {
  ef <- envfit_vectors(ord, phy_obj)
  # only pH is drawn from the environmental vectors (moisture / ground cover / depth stay in the csv)
  env_arr <- ef %>% filter(type == "vector", Variable == "pH") %>% mutate(label = Variable)
  veg_arr <- ef %>% filter(type == "Vegtype_indicator")
  # subtitle: the key comparison, pH vs Vegtype (full stats in the csv)
  sub_ph <- ef %>% filter(Variable == "pH")
  sub_veg <- ef %>% filter(Variable == "Vegtype", type == "factor")
  # p shown = block-restricted permutations (falls back to free permutations within a single block)
  subtitle <- paste0("envfit pH: r2=", round(sub_ph$r2, 2), ", p=", signif(sub_ph$p.value_strat, 2),
                     if (nrow(sub_veg) == 1) paste0(" | Vegtype: r2=", round(sub_veg$r2, 2), ", p=", signif(sub_veg$p.value_strat, 2)) else "",
                     if (n_distinct(data.frame(sample_data(phy_obj))$block) > 1) " (perm. within block)" else "")
  p +
    labs(subtitle = subtitle) +
    # pH arrow in black; vegtype arrows use the plot's Vegtype colour scale
    geom_segment(data = env_arr, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = x_plot, yend = y_plot),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), color = "black",
                 linewidth = 1) +
    geom_text(data = env_arr, aes(x = x_plot * 1.15, y = y_plot * 1.15, label = label),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = label_size, color = "black") +
    geom_segment(data = veg_arr, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = x_plot, yend = y_plot, color = Variable),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), linewidth = 1,
                 show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(data = veg_arr, aes(x = x_plot * 1.15, y = y_plot * 1.15, label = Variable, color = Variable),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = label_size, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE)
}
```

Function to throughoutput all the phyobj
```{r}
# Function to perform PCoA and NMDS ordinations and save plots
perform_ordinations <- function(phy_list, veg_colors) {
    # Create an empty list to store the plots
    plot_list <- list()
    
    for (phy_name in names(phy_list)) {
        phy_obj <- phy_list[[phy_name]]
        sample_data(phy_obj)$Vegtype <- factor(sample_data(phy_obj)$Vegtype)
        
        # Try to calculate the weighted UniFrac distance
        tryCatch({
            wunif_dist <- phyloseq::distance(phy_obj, method = "wunifrac")

            # Perform PCoA and NMDS ordinations
            #wunif_pcoa <- ordinate(phy_obj, method = "PCoA", distance = wunif_dist)
            wunif_NMDS <- ordinate(phy_obj, method = "NMDS", distance = wunif_dist)

            # Create the plots
            # plot_wu_pcoa <- plot_ordination(phy_obj, wunif_pcoa, color = "Vegtype", shape = "Location") +
            #                 scale_color_manual(values = veg_colors) +
            #                 ggtitle(paste0("PCoA - ", phy_name)) +
            #                 theme(legend.position = "none",
            #                       plot.title = element_text(size=12),
            #                       axis.title.x = element_text(size=8),
            #                       axis.title.y = element_text(size=8))

            plot_wu_NMDS <- plot_ordination(phy_obj, wunif_NMDS, color = "Vegtype", shape = "Location") +
                            scale_color_manual(values = veg_colors) +
                            theme(legend.position = "none",                                   
                                  plot.title = element_text(size=12),
                                  axis.title.x = element_text(size=8),
                                  axis.title.y = element_text(size=8)) +
                            ggtitle(paste0("NMDS - ", phy_name))

            # envfit pH + is_conifer arrows (falls back to the bare plot if the fit fails on a tiny subset)
            plot_wu_NMDS <- tryCatch(
                add_envfit_vectors(plot_wu_NMDS, wunif_NMDS, phy_obj, label_size = 2),
                error = function(e) {
                    message("envfit skipped for ", phy_name, ": ", e$message)
                    plot_wu_NMDS
                })

            # Save the plots in the list
            plot_list[[phy_name]] <- list(#plot_wu_pcoa, 
                                          plot_wu_NMDS)

            # Save the plots to files (you can remove this if not needed)
            #ggsave(paste0("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/contigs/Betadiv/",phy_name,"_plt_", "wu_PCoA.svg", device = svglite::svglite,), plot_wu_pcoa)
            ggsave(paste0("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/contigs/Betadiv/", phy_name, "_plt_wu_NMDS.svg"), plot_wu_NMDS, device = svglite::svglite)

        }, error = function(e) {
            message("Error in processing ", phy_name, ": ", e$message)
        })
    }
    
    return(plot_list)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to produce tables
table_maker <- function(adonis_res, filename_prefix) {
  
  # Extract the ANOVA table
  anova_table <- as.data.frame(adonis_res)
  
  # Create a data frame for R2 and p-values
  results_df <- anova_table %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    select(R2 = `R2`, p.value = `Pr(>F)`) %>%
    rownames_to_column(var = "Variable") %>%
    filter(Variable != "sample_data(phy_norm_f)$XK_ppm", Variable != "Residual", Variable != "Total")
  
  # Clean up the variable names
  results_df$Variable <- gsub("sample_data\\(phy_norm_f\\)\\$", "", results_df$Variable)
  results_df$Variable <- gsub("Vegtype:pH", "Vegtype * pH", results_df$Variable)
  results_df$R2 <- round(results_df$R2, digits = 2)
  
  # Display the table
  print(results_df)
  
  # Save the table as CSV
  csv_filename <- paste0(filename_prefix, ".csv")
  write.csv(results_df, file = csv_filename, row.names = FALSE)
  
  # Create a gt table
  gt_table <- gt(results_df) %>%
    tab_header(
      title = md("**Permanova Results**"),
      subtitle = filename_prefix
    )
  
  # Save the gt table as an image
  image_filename <- paste0("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Write_up/Main figures/",filename_prefix,"_fancy_table.pdf")
  gtsave(gt_table, filename = image_filename)
  
  return(results_df)
}

Uni_strat_results <- table_maker(Uni_adonis_strat, "Uni_adonis_strat")
```

##### Permanova, univariate-ordered (by = "terms")
```{r}
# Ported from Drydown 050826_metaT_gene_analyses_205.Rmd (~L309). Each term is tested alone
# (single-term adonis2, so its R2 doesn't depend on formula order), ranked by R2 desc (ties ->
# p desc), and that rank sets the term order for the sequential by = "terms" model, so the
# biggest driver gets first claim on shared variance. Same UniFrac / weighted UniFrac distances,
# variables, and block stratification as the chunk above.
set.seed(420)
wunif_dist <- phyloseq::distance(phy_norm_f, method = "wunifrac")
unif_dist <- phyloseq::distance(phy_norm_f, method = "unifrac")

perm_meta <- data.frame(sample_data(phy_norm_f))
# Surface geology isn't in the phyloseq sample_data; join it from the geology metadata by sample name

stopifnot(identical(rownames(perm_meta), labels(wunif_dist)),
          identical(rownames(perm_meta), labels(unif_dist)))

run_ordered_permanova <- function(dist_obj, meta, terms, label, strata = NULL, seed = 420) {
  uni <- purrr::map_dfr(terms, function(tm) {
    set.seed(seed)
    res <- adonis2(as.formula(paste("dist_obj ~", tm)), data = meta,
                   permutations = 999, strata = strata)
    tibble(model = label, Variable = tm, R2 = res$R2[1], p.value = res$`Pr(>F)`[1])
  })
  term_order <- uni %>% arrange(desc(R2), desc(p.value)) %>% pull(Variable)

  set.seed(seed)
  res <- adonis2(as.formula(paste("dist_obj ~", paste(term_order, collapse = " + "))),
                 data = meta, permutations = 999, by = "terms", strata = strata)
  list(univariate = uni, adonis = res)
}

perm_terms <- c("Vegtype", "pH", "Location", "depth", "perc_moist", "GroundCoverPerc", "Surface.Geology", "block")
perm_terms_strat <- setdiff(perm_terms, "block")

Uni_ord_strat <- run_ordered_permanova(unif_dist, perm_meta, perm_terms_strat, "Uni_adonis_strat_ordered", strata = perm_meta$block)
```

```{r}
#### Conifer vs other, ordered sequential ANOVAs
# Tidy a sequential (type I) aov. summary.aov pads row names with trailing spaces, so trimws()
# them (exact-name indexing like ["Vegtype", ...] silently returns NA otherwise).
# eta2 = SS_term / SS_total, the ANOVA analog of the PERMANOVA R2.
aov_tidy <- function(fit, model_label) {
  s <- summary(fit)[[1]]
  data.frame(model = model_label,
             Variable = trimws(rownames(s)),
             Df = s$Df,
             eta2 = s$`Sum Sq` / sum(s$`Sum Sq`),
             F = s$`F value`,
             p.value = s$`Pr(>F)`) %>%
    filter(Variable != "Residuals")
}

# Same ordering rule as the ordered PERMANOVA: each main effect alone, ranked by eta2 desc
# (ties -> p desc). That order feeds the sequential model; the interaction always comes last.
order_aov_terms <- function(terms, data, response = "pH") {
  purrr::map_dfr(terms, function(tm) aov_tidy(aov(as.formula(paste(response, "~", tm)), data = data), tm)) %>%
    arrange(desc(eta2), desc(p.value)) %>%
    pull(Variable)
}

run_ordered_aov <- function(terms, data = sampledata, response = "pH") {
  rhs <- paste(order_aov_terms(terms, data, response), collapse = " * ")
  aov_tidy(aov(as.formula(paste(response, "~", rhs)), data = data), rhs)
}

# Is the conifer pH effect bigger on a particular geology / block? delta = conifer - other mean pH
conifer_delta <- function(group_col) {
  sampledata %>%
    group_by(.data[[group_col]]) %>%
    summarise(n_conifer = sum(is_conifer == "Y"),
              n_other = sum(is_conifer == "N"),
              pH_conifer = mean(pH[is_conifer == "Y"]),
              pH_other = mean(pH[is_conifer == "N"]),
              delta_pH = pH_conifer - pH_other,
              p.value = if (n_conifer >= 2 && n_other >= 2) t.test(pH[is_conifer == "Y"], pH[is_conifer == "N"])$p.value else NA_real_,
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !starts_with("n_"), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
}

# Fixed x slots (other = left, conifer = right) instead of position_jitterdodge: jitterdodge groups
# by fill x block colour, which dropped some points into the wrong box (e.g. U_1 conifers in Km),

geo_levels <- sort(unique(sampledata$Surface.Geology))

  mutate(x_pos = match(Surface.Geology, geo_levels) + ifelse(is_conifer == "Y", 0.2, -0.2))

# Conifer vs other within each geology, accounting for block: lm(pH ~ block + is_conifer) on that
# geology's samples (block dropped where the geology is a single block). Stars use raw p (BH padj kept in the csv).
# Caveat: conifers are one plot per block (2 depths), so this still treats depths as replicates.
conifer_geo_block_adj <- purrr::map_dfr(geo_levels, function(g) {
  d <- sampledata %>% filter(Surface.Geology == g) %>% droplevels()
  if (n_distinct(d$is_conifer) < 2) return(tibble(Surface.Geology = g, estimate = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_))
  f <- if (n_distinct(d$block) > 1) pH ~ block + is_conifer else pH ~ is_conifer
  co <- summary(lm(f, data = d))$coefficients
  tibble(Surface.Geology = g, estimate = co["is_coniferY", "Estimate"], p.value = co["is_coniferY", "Pr(>|t|)"])
}) %>%
  mutate(padj = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH"),
         stars = case_when(is.na(p.value) ~ "", p.value < 0.001 ~ "***", p.value < 0.01 ~ "**", p.value < 0.05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "ns"))
print(conifer_geo_block_adj)
```

```{r}
phy_raw <- readRDS("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/Taxonomy/phyloseq_raw_count_object.rds")

#Subset for location

sample_data(phy_raw_hw)

phy_raw_lr <- subset_samples(phy_raw, Location == "lowerreaches")


#Set up taxa table
taxa_table <- as.data.frame(tax_table(phy_raw))
taxa_table <- rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(taxa_table), var = "OTU")


# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(420)

# Convert phyloseq object to DESeq2 object
dds <- phyloseq_to_deseq2(phy_raw, ~ Vegtype)
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# Reorder veg_types to ensure Conifer is processed first
veg_types <- levels(dds$Vegtype)

# Define the order of comparisons
comparisons_order <- list(
    c("Aspen", "Conifer"),
    c("Meadow", "Conifer"),
    c("Sagebrush", "Conifer"),
    c("Meadow", "Aspen"),
    c("Sagebrush", "Aspen"),
    c("Sagebrush", "Meadow")
)

# Initialize an empty list to store results
pairwise_results <- list()
significant_results <- list()
significant_taxa <- list()

# Loop through the predefined comparisons
for (comparison in comparisons_order) {
    var1 <- comparison[1]
    var2 <- comparison[2]
    comp_label <- paste(var1, "_vs_", var2)
    cat("Comparison: ", comp_label, "\n")
    
    res <- results(dds, contrast=c("Vegtype", var1, var2))
    resOrdered <- res[order(res$padj, na.last = NA),]
    pairwise_results[[comp_label]] <- resOrdered
    
    # Subset the results for significant values
    significant_res <- subset(resOrdered, padj < 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) > 1)
    significant_results[[comp_label]] <- significant_res
    sig_df <- as.data.frame(significant_results[[comp_label]])
    sig_df <- rownames_to_column(sig_df, var = "OTU")
    
    # Add columns for var1 and var2
    sig_df$var1 <- var1
    sig_df$var2 <- var2
    
    # Reorder columns to have OTU, var1, var2, log2FoldChange, padj at the beginning
    sig_df <- sig_df %>% select(OTU, var1, var2, log2FoldChange, padj, everything())
    
    # Merge significant results with taxonomic information
    significant_taxa[[comp_label]] <- left_join(sig_df, taxa_table, by = "OTU")
    print(head(significant_taxa[[comp_label]]))
}
```

###### Updated phylum and family counts
```{r}

# Initialize an empty dataframe to store phylum counts
phylum_counts <- data.frame(Comparison = character(), Variable = character(), Phylum = character(), Count = integer(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


for (comparison in names(significant_taxa)) {
  # Extract the significant results for the comparison
  significant_res <- significant_taxa[[comparison]]
  print(paste("Processing comparison:", comparison))
  
  # Separate based on log2FoldChange sign
  positive_res <- significant_res %>% filter(log2FoldChange > 0)
  negative_res <- significant_res %>% filter(log2FoldChange < 0)
  
  # Extract variables from comparison string
  vars <- unlist(strsplit(comparison, "_vs_"))
  var1 <- vars[1]
  var2 <- vars[2]
  
  print(paste("var1 (positive log2FC):", var1))
  print(paste("var2 (negative log2FC):", var2))
  
  # Count the occurrences of each phylum for positive log2FoldChange
  phylum_count_pos <- positive_res %>% 
    group_by(Phylum) %>% 
    summarize(Count = n()) %>% 
    mutate(Variable = var1) # Positive log2FoldChange means more associated with var1
  
  # Count the occurrences of each phylum for negative log2FoldChange
  phylum_count_neg <- negative_res %>% 
    group_by(Phylum) %>% 
    summarize(Count = n()) %>% 
    mutate(Variable = var2) # Negative log2FoldChange means more associated with var2
  
  print("Phylum counts for positive log2FC:")
  print(phylum_count_pos)
  
  print("Phylum counts for negative log2FC:")
  print(phylum_count_neg)
  
  # Add a column for the comparison
  phylum_count_pos$Comparison <- comparison
  phylum_count_neg$Comparison <- comparison
  
  # Combine with the main dataframe
  phylum_counts <- rbind(phylum_counts, phylum_count_pos, phylum_count_neg)
}
```

```{r}
# Loop through significant results to count family occurrences

  # Extract the significant results for the comparison

  # Separate based on log2FoldChange sign
  positive_res <- significant_res %>% filter(log2FoldChange > 0)
  negative_res <- significant_res %>% filter(log2FoldChange < 0)
  
  # Extract variables from comparison string
  vars <- unlist(strsplit(comparison, "_vs_"))
  var1 <- vars[1]
  var2 <- vars[2]
  
  # Count the occurrences of each family for positive log2FoldChange
  family_count_pos <- positive_res %>% 
    group_by(Family) %>% 
    summarize(Count = n()) %>% 
    mutate(Variable = var1) # Positive log2FoldChange means more associated with var1
  
  # Count the occurrences of each family for negative log2FoldChange
  family_count_neg <- negative_res %>% 
    group_by(Family) %>% 
    summarize(Count = n()) %>% 
    mutate(Variable = var2) # Negative log2FoldChange means more associated with var2
```

# Sample Analysis

Main goal: show correlation between vegtype and trait data. Perhaps Ill use the approach that Jackie takes here: https://jkzorz.github.io/2019/06/11/Correlation-heatmaps.html.

Subset the sample_trait_data by trait category (so Resource Aqusition, Stress Tolerance, Resource Use). Then do a correlation plot on each by the number of samples, and cluster both the samples and the traits to see if samples cluster by vegtype, or not.

## Normalization and Visualization of sample traits
#### Analysis of variance for all sample traits
```{r}
sample_trait_data <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/031023_sample_trait_coverage.csv", header = T)
metadata <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/VegType_explanitory_variables.csv")

sample_trait_data_joined <- left_join(sample_trait_data, metadata, by = "sample")
sample_trait_data <- sample_trait_data_joined %>%
  mutate(block = block.y) %>%
  select(c(sample, vegtype, location, block, pH, everything()))

ncol(sample_trait_data)
sample_trait_data_nocov <- sample_trait_data %>%
    select(c(sample, vegtype, location, block, pH, 6:140))
ncol(sample_trait_data_nocov)

# Initialize a data frame to store results
results <- data.frame(
  Trait = character(),
  Vegtype_Fstat = numeric(),
  Vegtype_pvalue = numeric(),
  pH_Fstat = numeric(),
  pH_pvalue = numeric(),
  Block_Fstat = numeric(),
  Block_pvalue = numeric(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop through each trait column and perform ANOVA
for (i in 6:ncol(sample_trait_data_nocov)) {
  trait <- colnames(sample_trait_data_nocov)[i]
  formula <- as.formula(paste(trait, "~ vegtype + pH + block"))
  anova_result <- aov(formula, data = sample_trait_data_nocov)
  summary_result <- summary(anova_result)
  
  # Extract F-statistics and p-values
  vegtype_Fstat <- summary_result[[1]]$`F value`[1]
  vegtype_pvalue <- summary_result[[1]]$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  pH_Fstat <- summary_result[[1]]$`F value`[2]
  pH_pvalue <- summary_result[[1]]$`Pr(>F)`[2]
  block_Fstat <- summary_result[[1]]$`F value`[3]
  block_pvalue <- summary_result[[1]]$`Pr(>F)`[3]
  
  # Add to results data frame
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
    Trait = trait,
    Vegtype_Fstat = vegtype_Fstat,
    Vegtype_pvalue = vegtype_pvalue,
    pH_Fstat = pH_Fstat,
    pH_pvalue = pH_pvalue,
    Block_Fstat = block_Fstat,
    Block_pvalue = block_pvalue,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

sample_trait_anova_results <- results

# Display the results
print((results))
```

#### Heatmaps

##### Norm heatmap
```{r}
normalized_sample_trait_data <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/Nov2024_normalized_sample_trait_matrix.csv", row.names = 1)
# Z-score normalization for columns 83 to 182, handling NaN and Inf values
normalized_sample_trait_data_zscore <- normalized_sample_trait_data %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(7:141)), ~scale(.)[,1]) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(7:141)), ~ifelse(!is.finite(.), min(., na.rm = TRUE), .)) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(7:141)), ~replace(., is.infinite(.), min(., is.finite(.)))) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample))

# Filter for duplicates and choose the one with the highest SumCoverage value
map_filtered <- normalized_sample_trait_data_zscore %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample)) %>%
  arrange(desc(vegtype)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample)) %>%  # Ensure there are no missing values in sample
  distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%  # Remove any duplicate samples
  column_to_rownames(var = "sample") %>%
  select(6:140) %>%
  mutate_all(~replace(., is.na(.), 0))

# Remove columns where every value is zero for cleaner showing
map_normalized <- map_filtered %>%
  select_if(~!all(. == 0))

# Prepare the annotation dataframe
annotation <- normalized_sample_trait_data_zscore %>%
  mutate(vegtype = factor(vegtype)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample)) %>%  # Ensure there are no missing values in sample
  distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%  # Remove any duplicate samples
  column_to_rownames(var = "sample") %>%
  select(vegtype)

# Define colors for vegtype and block
veg_colors <- c("aspen" = "#FFC125", "conifer" = "#6E8B3D", "meadow" = "#DDA0DD", "sage" = "#CD5B45")
block_colors <- brewer.pal(9, "Pastel1")
names(block_colors) <- c("H_1", "H_2", "H_3", "L_1", "L_2", "L_3", "U_1", "U_2", "U_3")

# Prepare the annotation dataframe
annotation <- normalized_sample_trait_data_zscore %>%
  mutate(vegtype = factor(vegtype),
         block = factor(block)) %>%  # Ensure block is a factor
  filter(!is.na(sample)) %>%  # Ensure there are no missing values in sample
  distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%  # Remove any duplicate samples
  column_to_rownames(var = "sample") %>%
  select(vegtype, block, pH)

# Create a list for annotation colors
annotation_colors <- list(vegtype = veg_colors, block = block_colors)

# Assuming map_normalized has already been created
# Convert the data to a matrix for pheatmap
map_matrix <- as.matrix(map_normalized)

# Transpose the matrix
```

####### View arranged by vegtype
```{r}
# Z-score normalization for columns, handling NaN and Inf values
normalized_sample_trait_data_zscore <- normalized_sample_trait_data %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(9:143)), ~scale(.)[,1]) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(9:143)), ~ifelse(!is.finite(.), min(., na.rm = TRUE), .)) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(9:143)), ~replace(., is.infinite(.), min(., is.finite(.)))) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample))

# Filter for duplicates and choose the one with the highest SumCoverage value
map_filtered <- normalized_sample_trait_data_zscore %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample)) %>%
  arrange(desc(vegtype)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample)) %>%  # Ensure there are no missing values in sample
  distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%  # Remove any duplicate samples
  column_to_rownames(var = "sample") %>%
  select(9:143, -Location.x) %>%
  mutate_all(~replace(., is.na(.), 0))

# Remove columns where every value is zero for cleaner showing
map_normalized <- map_filtered %>%
  select_if(~!all(. == 0))


# Prepare the annotation dataframe
annotation <- normalized_sample_trait_data_zscore %>%
  mutate(vegtype = factor(vegtype),
         elevation_category = factor(elevation_category),
         depth = factor(depth)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample)) %>%
  distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "sample") %>%
  select(vegtype, elevation_category, depth)

# Define colors for vegtype and elevation_category
veg_colors <- c("aspen" = "#FFC125", "conifer" = "#6E8B3D", "meadow" = "#DDA0DD", "sage" = "#CD5B45")
elevation_colors <- c("Low" = "#87CEFA", "High" = "#FF6347", "Unknown" = "#CCCCCC")
depth_colors <- c("1" = "#FFFFFF", "2" = "#000000")

# Create a list for annotation colors
annotation_colors <- list(vegtype = veg_colors, elevation_category = elevation_colors, depth = depth_colors)

# Convert the data to a matrix for pheatmap
map_matrix <- as.matrix(map_normalized)

# Transpose the matrix
transposed_matrix <- t(map_matrix)


# Update the pheatmap function call
pheatmap(transposed_matrix, show_rownames = TRUE, 
         show_colnames = TRUE,
         cluster_rows = F,
         cluster_cols = T,
         annotation_col = annotation,
         annotation_colors = annotation_colors,
         annotation_legend_side = "right",
         main = "Sample Trait Zscores Weighted by Coverage + Vegtype ANOVA BH Padj",
         fontsize = 25,
         breaks = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 100),

         filename = "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/NOV2024_normalized/zscore_sample_traits_test2.png", width = 45, height = 40)
```

```{r}
# Add significance levels to traits

    TRUE ~ ""
```

###### Make the data
```{r}
# Load your data
sample_trait_data <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/031023_sample_trait_coverage.csv", header = TRUE)
metadata_wgeology_new <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/metadata_wgeology_new.csv", sep = ",", row.names = 1)

#Okay lets just assign elevation information:
Low_elev <- c("U_1", "U_3", "L_1", "L_2")
High_elev <- c("H_1", "H_2", "H_3", "U_2", "L_3")

# Join the sample_trait_data with metadata
sample_trait_data_joined <- left_join(sample_trait_data, metadata_wgeology_new, by = "sample")
sample_trait_data <- sample_trait_data_joined %>%
  mutate(block = block.y) %>% 
  mutate(depth = depth.y) %>%
  mutate(elevation_category = case_when(
    block %in% Low_elev ~ "Low",
    block %in% High_elev ~ "High",
    TRUE ~ "Unknown")) %>%
  select(c(sample, vegtype, elevation_category, depth, pH, everything()))
ncol(sample_trait_data)
```
###### View aranged by vegtype
```{r}
# Z-score normalization for columns 83 to 182, handling NaN and Inf values
sample_trait_data_zscore <- sample_trait_data %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(5:140)), ~scale(.)[,1]) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(5:140)), ~ifelse(!is.finite(.), min(., na.rm = TRUE), .)) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(5:140)), ~replace(., is.infinite(.), min(., is.finite(.)))) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample))

# Filter for duplicates and choose the one with the highest SumCoverage value
map_filtered <- sample_trait_data_zscore %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample)) %>%
  arrange(desc(vegtype)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample)) %>%  # Ensure there are no missing values in sample
  distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%  # Remove any duplicate samples
  column_to_rownames(var = "sample") %>%
  select(5:140) %>%
  mutate_all(~replace(., is.na(.), 0))

# Remove columns where every value is zero for cleaner showing
map_normalized <- map_filtered %>%
  select_if(~!all(. == 0))

# Prepare the annotation dataframe
annotation <- sample_trait_data_zscore %>%
  mutate(vegtype = factor(vegtype),
         elevation_category = factor(elevation_category),
         depth = factor(depth)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample)) %>%
  distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "sample") %>%
  select(vegtype, elevation_category, depth)

# Define colors for vegtype and elevation_category
veg_colors <- c("aspen" = "#FFC125", "conifer" = "#6E8B3D", "meadow" = "#DDA0DD", "sage" = "#CD5B45")
elevation_colors <- c("Low" = "#87CEFA", "High" = "#FF6347", "Unknown" = "#CCCCCC")
depth_colors <- c("1" = "#FFFFFF", "2" = "#000000")

# Create a list for annotation colors
annotation_colors <- list(vegtype = veg_colors, elevation_category = elevation_colors, depth = depth_colors)

# Update the pheatmap function call
pheatmap(transposed_matrix, show_rownames = TRUE, 
         show_colnames = TRUE,
         cluster_rows = F,
         cluster_cols = T,
         annotation_col = annotation,
         annotation_colors = annotation_colors,
         annotation_legend_side = "right",
         main = "Sample Trait Zscores Weighted by Coverage + Vegtype ANOVA BH Padj",
         fontsize = 25,
         breaks = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 100),
         color = viridis(100),
         filename = "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/zscore_sample_traits_test2.png", width = 45, height = 40)
```

```{r}
subset_data <- sample_trait_data %>%
  select(sample, 7:193)

# Function to clean up column names
clean_colname <- function(colname) {
  for (trait in level1_traits) {
    if (grepl(trait, colname, fixed = TRUE)) {
      return(trait)
    }
  }
  return(colname)
}

# Subset the data
subset_data <- sample_trait_data %>%
  select(sample, 7:193)

# Clean up the column names
cleaned_names <- sapply(names(subset_data)[-1], clean_colname)
names(subset_data)[-1] <- cleaned_names

# Group and sum the columns with the same cleaned names

  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(across(-sample, sum, na.rm = TRUE))

# Merge back with the original metadata
sample_microtrait_lvl1 <- sample_trait_data %>%
  select(1:6) %>%
  left_join(sample_microtrait_lvl1, by = "sample")
```

## Individual Traits and Taxa 

#### Chitinase plot
```{r}
normalized_sample_trait_data <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/Nov2024_normalized_sample_trait_matrix.csv", row.names = 1)

block_colors <- c("#1F77B4", "#FF7F0E", "#2CA02C", "#D62728", "#9467BD", "#8C564B", "#E377C2", "#7F7F7F", "#BCBD22")
names(block_colors) <- c("H_1", "H_2", "H_3", "L_1", "L_2", "L_3", "U_1", "U_2", "U_3")
veg_colors <- c("Aspen" = "#FFC125", "Conifer" = "#6E8B3D", "Meadow" = "#DDA0DD", "Sagebrush" = "#CD5B45")
normalized_sample_trait_data$Location <- as.factor(normalized_sample_trait_data$Location)
normalized_sample_trait_data$Vegtype <- as.factor(normalized_sample_trait_data$Vegtype)
normalized_sample_trait_data$block <- as.factor(normalized_sample_trait_data$block)

set.seed(420)
# Model
anova_result <- aov(Resource.Acquisition.Substrate.degradation.complex.carbohydrate.depolymerization.chitin.breakdown ~ Vegtype + pH + block, data = normalized_sample_trait_data)

anova_summary_interaction <- summary(anova_result)
p_value_vegtype <- anova_summary_interaction[[1]]["vegtype", "Pr(>F)"]
p_value_block <- anova_summary_interaction[[1]]["block", "Pr(>F)"]
p_value_pH <- anova_summary_interaction[[1]]["pH", "Pr(>F)"]

# Plot: Boxplots by Vegetation Type, Points colored by block
plot_veg <- ggplot(normalized_normalized_sample_trait_data, row.names = 1, aes(x = sample, y = Resource.Acquisition.Substrate.degradation.complex.carbohydrate.depolymerization.chitin.breakdown, color = Vegtype, shape = Location)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = veg_colors) +
  labs(title = "Chitin breakdown Distribution by Vegetation Type",
       subtitle = paste("p-value (Vegtype):", signif(p_value_vegtype, digits = 3),
                        " | p-value (pH):", signif(p_value_pH, digits = 3)),
       x = "sample", y = "Chitinase abundance") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

print(plot_veg)
ggsave("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/chitinase/plot_samples_chitinase.svg", device = svglite::svglite, plot = plot_veg,dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# Plot: Boxplots by Vegetation Type, colored points by block
plot_veg_box <- ggplot(normalized_normalized_sample_trait_data, aes(x = Vegtype, y = Resource.Acquisition.Substrate.degradation.complex.carbohydrate.depolymerization.chitin.breakdown, fill = Vegtype)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = block), size = 2, width = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = veg_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = block_colors) +
  labs(title = "Chitin breakdown Distribution by Vegetation Type",
       subtitle = paste("p-value (Vegtype):", signif(p_value_vegtype, digits = 3),
                        " | p-value (pH):", signif(p_value_pH, digits = 3),
                        " | p-value (block):", signif(p_value_block, digits = 3)),
       x = "sample", y = "Chitinase abundance") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

print(plot_veg_box)
ggsave("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/chitinase/plot_veg_box_chitinase.svg", device = svglite::svglite, plot = plot_veg_box,dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

##### Relative abundance of Chitinophagaceae in my dataset
```{r}
# Filter for Chitinophagaceae family
Chitinophagaceae <- subset_taxa(phy_norm, Family == "Chitinophagaceae")

# Calculate relative abundance relative to the entire community
rel_abund <- transform_sample_counts(phy_norm, function(x) x / sum(x))
rel_abund_Chitinophagaceae <- prune_taxa(taxa_names(Chitinophagaceae), rel_abund)

# Extract sample data
sample_data_df <- data.frame(sample_data(phy_norm))
sample_data_df$Sample <- rownames(sample_data_df)

# Calculate summed relative abundance and coverage
final_results <- data.frame(
  Sample = sample_names(rel_abund_Chitinophagaceae),
  rel_abund = colSums(otu_table(rel_abund_Chitinophagaceae)),
  coverage = colSums(otu_table(Chitinophagaceae))
)

final_results <- final_results %>%
  left_join(sample_data_df, by = "Sample") %>%
  group_by(Vegtype) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_rel_abund = mean(rel_abund),
    total_rel_abund = sum(rel_abund),
    coverage_sum = sum(coverage),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(final_results)

# Optionally, save the results to a CSV file
write.csv(final_results, "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/Abundance of Certain Taxa per vegtype/Chitinophagaceae_abundance_coverage.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Function to create a boxplot for a single trait
create_boxplot <- function(data, trait) {
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = "Vegtype", y = trait, fill = "Vegtype")) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(aes(color = block), size = 0.5, width = 0.2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = veg_colors) +
    scale_color_manual(values = block_colors) +
    labs(title = gsub("\\.", " ", trait),
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 6),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.position = "none")
}

# Create a list of plots
plot_list <- lapply(traits, function(trait) create_boxplot(sample_trait_data, trait))

# Combine all plots
combined_plot <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 3)  # Adjust ncol as needed

# Add a title to the entire figure
final_plot <- combined_plot + 
  plot_annotation(title = "Nitrogen-Related Trait Distributions by Vegetation Type",
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16)))

# Save the combined plot
ggsave("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/nitrogen_traits_boxplots.svg", device = svglite::svglite, 
       final_plot, width = 20, height = 25, dpi = 300, limitsize = FALSE)

# Display the plot (optional)
```

##### Sacchari abundances
```{r}
# Filter for Steroidobacteraceae family
Saccharibacteria <- subset_taxa(phy_norm, Phylum == "Candidatus Saccharibacteria")

# Calculate relative abundance relative to the entire community
rel_abund <- transform_sample_counts(phy_norm, function(x) x / sum(x))
rel_abund_Saccharibacteria <- prune_taxa(taxa_names(Saccharibacteria), rel_abund)

# Extract sample data
sample_data_df <- data.frame(sample_data(phy_norm))
sample_data_df$Sample <- rownames(sample_data_df)

# Calculate summed relative abundance and coverage
final_results <- data.frame(
  Sample = sample_names(rel_abund_Saccharibacteria),
  rel_abund = colSums(otu_table(rel_abund_Saccharibacteria)),
  coverage = colSums(otu_table(Saccharibacteria))
)

final_results <- final_results %>%
  left_join(sample_data_df, by = "Sample") %>%
  group_by(Vegtype) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_rel_abund = mean(rel_abund),
    total_rel_abund = sum(rel_abund),
    coverage_sum = sum(coverage),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(final_results)

# Optionally, save the results to a CSV file
write.csv(final_results, "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/Abundance of Certain Taxa per vegtype/Saccharibacteria_abundance_coverage.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

###### Lignin normalized analysis
```{r}
curated_bin_trait_lignin <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/curated_bin_trait_lignin.csv")

# Assuming your merged dataframe is called 'merged_df'
long_df <- curated_bin_trait_lignin %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 17:82, 
               names_to = "sample", 
               values_to = "Coverage") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Lignin.peroxidase)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(laccase))

# Check the result
head(long_df)
str(long_df)

  # Step 2: Calculate weighted enzyme values
weighted_df <- long_df %>%
  mutate(Weighted_Laccase = laccase * Coverage,
         Weighted_Lignin_Peroxidase = Lignin.peroxidase * Coverage)

# Check the result
head(weighted_df[126:127])
weighted_df_view <- weighted_df %>%
  select(Genome, Phylum, Class, Weighted_Laccase, Weighted_Lignin_Peroxidase) %>%
  arrange(desc(Weighted_Laccase))

  
  # Step 3: Sum weighted values for each enzyme across bins for each sample
sample_weighted_lignin_values <- weighted_df %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(Laccase = sum(Weighted_Laccase),
            Lignin_Peroxidase = sum(Weighted_Lignin_Peroxidase))

# Check the result
head(sample_weighted_lignin_values)

#Normalize the sample weighted lignin values
bam_stats <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Microtrait/coverm_genome/bam_stats_updated_Nov2024.csv")
bam_stats

# Arrange the Files by the third character
bam_stats <- bam_stats %>%
  mutate(third_char = substr(sample, 3, 3)) %>%
  arrange(third_char, sample) %>%
  select(sample, Mapped.Reads)  # remove the helper column

# Convert sample to a factor with the correct order
bam_stats$sample <- factor(bam_stats$sample, levels = bam_stats$sample)

#Combine the dfs and do some subtraction to get a new column
combined_sample_weighted_lignin_values <- left_join(sample_weighted_lignin_values, bam_stats, by = "sample")

# Normalize each trait value by the unmapped_reads value for that sample
norm_sample_weighted_lignin_values <- combined_sample_weighted_lignin_values %>%
  mutate(across(2:3, ~ . / Mapped.Reads)) %>%
  select(sample, Laccase, Lignin_Peroxidase)
```

```{r}
# Z-score normalization for columns 83 to 182, handling NaN and Inf values
lignin_mat_zscore <- lignin_mat %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(1:109)), ~scale(.)[,1]) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(c(1:109)), ~ifelse(!is.finite(.), min(., na.rm = TRUE), .)) %>%

pheatmap(transposed_lignin_matrix,

         show_colnames = TRUE,
         cluster_rows = F,
         cluster_cols = T,
         fontsize = 10,
         breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 100),  # Adjust the breaks to cap the Z-scores
         color = viridis(100),
         main = "Microbial Trait Heatmap",
         filename = "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/Bin_traits/lignin_trait_heatmap_noclust.svg", device = svglite::svglite, 
         width = 30, 
         height = 15)

# Assuming Bin_weighted_lignin_values is your dataframe
# and Laccase is the column we're interested in
# Remove rows with zero Laccase values
non_zero_laccase <- Bin_weighted_lignin_values[Bin_weighted_lignin_values$Laccase > 0, ]
# Richness
richness <- nrow(non_zero_laccase)
# Shannon Index
shannon <- diversity(non_zero_laccase$Laccase, index = "shannon")
# Simpson Index
simpson <- diversity(non_zero_laccase$Laccase, index = "simpson")
# Pielou's Evenness
evenness <- shannon / log(richness)
# Print results
cat("Richness:", richness, "\n")
cat("Shannon Index:", shannon, "\n")
cat("Simpson Index:", simpson, "\n")
cat("Pielou's Evenness:", evenness, "\n")

# Remove rows with zero Lignin_Peroxidase values
non_zero_Lignin_Peroxidase <- Bin_weighted_lignin_values[Bin_weighted_lignin_values$Lignin_Peroxidase > 0, ]
# Richness
richness <- nrow(non_zero_Lignin_Peroxidase)
# Shannon Index
shannon <- diversity(non_zero_Lignin_Peroxidase$Lignin_Peroxidase, index = "shannon")
# Simpson Index
simpson <- diversity(non_zero_Lignin_Peroxidase$Lignin_Peroxidase, index = "simpson")
# Pielou's Evenness
evenness <- shannon / log(richness)
# Print results
cat("Richness:", richness, "\n")
cat("Shannon Index:", shannon, "\n")
cat("Simpson Index:", simpson, "\n")
cat("Pielou's Evenness:", evenness, "\n")
```

##### Relative abundance of steroidobacter in my dataset
```{r}
# Filter for Steroidobacteraceae family
steroidobacteraceae <- subset_taxa(phy_norm, Family == "Steroidobacteraceae")
tax_table(steroidobacteraceae)
# Calculate relative abundance relative to the entire community
rel_abund <- transform_sample_counts(phy_norm, function(x) x / sum(x))
rel_abund_steroidobacteraceae <- prune_taxa(taxa_names(steroidobacteraceae), rel_abund)

# Extract sample data
sample_data_df <- data.frame(sample_data(phy_norm))
sample_data_df$Sample <- rownames(sample_data_df)

# Calculate summed relative abundance and coverage
final_results <- data.frame(
  Sample = sample_names(rel_abund_steroidobacteraceae),
  rel_abund = colSums(otu_table(rel_abund_steroidobacteraceae)),
  coverage = colSums(otu_table(steroidobacteraceae))
)

final_results <- final_results %>%
  left_join(sample_data_df, by = "Sample") %>%
  group_by(Vegtype) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_rel_abund = mean(rel_abund),
    total_rel_abund = sum(rel_abund),
    coverage_sum = sum(coverage),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(final_results)

# Optionally, save the results to a CSV file
write.csv(final_results, "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/Abundance of Certain Taxa per vegtype/steroidobacteraceae_abundance_coverage.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

#### Consolidated heatmap
```{r}
# Load your data
curated_bin_trait_lignin <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/curated_bin_trait_lignin.csv")
combined_ordered_wbin <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/Taxonomy/deseq/combined_taxa_log2foldchange_traits copy.csv")


combine_bins_for_taxa <- function(taxa_name, curated_filter_col, curated_pattern, 
                                 deseq_filter_col, deseq_pattern) {
  
  # Get curated bins
  curated_bins <- curated_bin_trait_lignin %>%
    filter(grepl(curated_pattern, .data[[curated_filter_col]])) %>%
    mutate(source = "curated")
  
  # Get deseq bins
  deseq_bins <- combined_ordered_wbin %>%
    filter(grepl(deseq_pattern, .data[[deseq_filter_col]])) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Genome)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Resource.Acquisition.Substrate.uptake.aromatic.acid.transport)) %>%
    distinct(Genome, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    # Remove protein degradation column if present
    select(-any_of("Resource.Acquisition.Substrate.degradation.simple.compound.degradation.protein.degradation")) %>%
    mutate(source = "deseq")
  
  # Find common columns between datasets
  common_cols <- intersect(names(curated_bins), names(deseq_bins))
  
  # Select common columns and combine
  curated_subset <- curated_bins %>% select(all_of(common_cols))
  deseq_subset <- deseq_bins %>% select(all_of(common_cols))
  
  # Combine and remove duplicates based on Genome
  combined_bins <- bind_rows(curated_subset, deseq_subset) %>%
    distinct(Genome, .keep_all = TRUE)
  
  cat("Taxa:", taxa_name, "\n")
  cat("Curated bins:", nrow(curated_bins), "\n")
  cat("DESEQ bins:", nrow(deseq_bins), "\n")
  cat("Combined unique bins:", nrow(combined_bins), "\n")
  cat("Common columns:", length(common_cols), "\n\n")
  
  return(combined_bins)
}

plot_heatmap_for_bins <- function(combined_bins, taxa_name) {
  
  # Find trait columns (those starting with "Resource.")
  trait_cols <- grep("^Resource\\.", colnames(combined_bins))
  
  if(length(trait_cols) == 0) {
    cat("No trait columns found for", taxa_name, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Prepare trait matrix
  trait_mat <- combined_bins %>%
    column_to_rownames(var = "Genome") %>%
    select(all_of(trait_cols)) %>%
    as.matrix()
  
  # Remove traits (columns) that are all zeros
  non_zero_cols <- colSums(trait_mat != 0, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
  filtered_mat <- trait_mat[, non_zero_cols, drop = FALSE]
  
  if(ncol(filtered_mat) == 0) {
    cat("No non-zero traits found for", taxa_name, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Transpose so traits are rows and bins are columns
  heatmap_mat <- t(filtered_mat)
  
  # Prepare column annotations for the bins
  annotation_col <- combined_bins %>%
    filter(Genome %in% colnames(heatmap_mat)) %>%
    select(Genome, Phylum, source) %>%
    column_to_rownames(var = "Genome")
  
  # Ensure annotation rows match heatmap columns
  annotation_col <- annotation_col[colnames(heatmap_mat), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # Define colors for annotations
  source_colors <- c("curated" = "#1F78B4", "deseq" = "purple2")
  
  # Create phylum colors
  unique_phylums <- unique(annotation_col$Phylum)
  if(length(unique_phylums) > 0) {
    phylum_colors <- rainbow(length(unique_phylums))
    names(phylum_colors) <- unique_phylums
  } else {
    phylum_colors <- c("Unknown" = "#999999")
  }
  
  ann_colors <- list(
    source = source_colors,
    Phylum = phylum_colors
  )
  
  # Create heatmap
  pheatmap(heatmap_mat,
           cluster_rows = T,     # No clustering as requested
```

#### Non-parametric stats gran3 (New, April)
##### Normality check on ANCOVA residuals (GRAN3) — validate ANOVA assumption before Tukey
```{r normality_check_gran3}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)

# --- Reconstruct normalized_sample_trait_data from scratch ---
sample_trait_data <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/sample_trait_granularity3.csv", header = TRUE)
metadata <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/VegType_explanitory_variables.csv")

sample_trait_data <- left_join(sample_trait_data, metadata, by = "sample") %>%
  select(c(sample, Vegtype, Location, block, pH, everything()))

sample_trait_data_nocov <- sample_trait_data %>%
  select(c(sample, Vegtype, Location, block, pH, 7:194))

bam_stats <- read.csv("/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Microtrait/coverm_genome/bam_stats_updated_Nov2024.csv") %>%
  mutate(third_char = substr(sample, 3, 3)) %>%
  arrange(third_char, sample) %>%
  select(sample, Mapped.Reads)
bam_stats$sample <- factor(bam_stats$sample, levels = bam_stats$sample)

normalized_sample_trait_data <- left_join(sample_trait_data_nocov, bam_stats, by = "sample") %>%
  mutate(across(6:193, ~ . / Mapped.Reads)) %>%
  select(sample, Vegtype, Location, block, pH, Mapped.Reads, everything())

# --- Pool residuals across all trait columns for an overall QQ / histogram ---
trait_cols <- colnames(normalized_sample_trait_data)[7:ncol(normalized_sample_trait_data)]

all_residuals <- unlist(lapply(trait_cols, function(trait) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(trait, "~ Vegtype + pH + block"))
  resid(aov(formula, data = normalized_sample_trait_data))
}))

# Overall QQ plot of pooled residuals
qqnorm(all_residuals, main = "QQ Plot — Pooled ANCOVA Residuals (all traits, GRAN3)")
qqline(all_residuals, col = "red")

# Histogram of pooled residuals
hist(all_residuals, breaks = 60, main = "Histogram of Pooled ANCOVA Residuals (GRAN3)",
     xlab = "Residual", col = "steelblue", border = "white")

# --- Per-trait Shapiro-Wilk (supplementary formal test) ---
shapiro_results <- lapply(trait_cols, function(trait) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(trait, "~ Vegtype + pH + block"))
  resids <- resid(aov(formula, data = normalized_sample_trait_data))
  if (length(unique(resids)) == 1) {
    return(data.frame(Trait = trait, W = NA, p_value = NA, normal = NA, note = "zero-inflated (constant residuals)"))
  }
  sw <- shapiro.test(resids)
  data.frame(Trait = trait, W = sw$statistic, p_value = sw$p.value, normal = sw$p.value > 0.05, note = "ok")
})

shapiro_summary <- do.call(rbind, shapiro_results)
rownames(shapiro_summary) <- NULL

n_zero_inflated <- sum(shapiro_summary$note == "zero-inflated (constant residuals)")
n_testable      <- sum(shapiro_summary$note == "ok")
n_normal        <- sum(shapiro_summary$normal, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("%d of %d traits are zero-inflated (skipped)\n", n_zero_inflated, nrow(shapiro_summary)))
cat(sprintf("%d of %d testable traits have normally distributed residuals (Shapiro-Wilk p > 0.05)\n", n_normal, n_testable))

print(head(shapiro_summary, 20))

write.csv(shapiro_summary,
          "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/Trait_tables/shapiro_normality_ANCOVA_residuals_GRAN3.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

##### Non-parametric post-hoc: Kruskal-Wallis + Dunn's test (GRAN3 supplementary table)
```{r dunn_posthoc_gran3}
library(rstatix)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# Dunn's test per significant trait, with mean difference between groups
# Mean diff = mean(group1) - mean(group2) in normalized trait units (analogous to Tukey diff)
# p and p.adj from Dunn's test (BH correction across pairwise comparisons within each trait)
run_dunn_test <- function(trait) {
  if (length(unique(normalized_sample_trait_data[[trait]])) == 1) return(NULL)

  means <- normalized_sample_trait_data %>%
    group_by(Vegtype) %>%
    summarise(mean_val = mean(.data[[trait]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    deframe()

  dunn_test(normalized_sample_trait_data,
            as.formula(paste(trait, "~ Vegtype")),
            p.adjust.method = "BH") %>%
    mutate(
      Trait      = trait,
      Comparison = paste(group1, group2, sep = " - "),
      Mean_diff  = means[group1] - means[group2],
      enriched   = case_when(Mean_diff > 0 ~ group1,
                             Mean_diff < 0 ~ group2,
                             Mean_diff == 0 ~ "neither")
    ) %>%
    select(Trait, Comparison, Mean_diff, p_raw = p, p_adj = p.adj, enriched)
}

trait_cols <- colnames(normalized_sample_trait_data)[7:ncol(normalized_sample_trait_data)]
all_dunn_results <- map(trait_cols, run_dunn_test) %>% bind_rows()
dropped_traits <- trait_cols[!trait_cols %in% unique(all_dunn_results$Trait)]
cat(length(dropped_traits), "traits dropped (zero-inflated):\n")
print(dropped_traits)


# Wide format: one row per trait, columns grouped by comparison (diff / p_raw / p_adj / enriched)
comparisons <- unique(all_dunn_results$Comparison)

col_order <- c("Trait", unlist(lapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
  c(paste0(comp, "__Mean_diff"),
    paste0(comp, "__p_raw"),
    paste0(comp, "__p_adj"),
    paste0(comp, "__enriched"))
})))

dunn_wide <- all_dunn_results %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Comparison,
              values_from = c(Mean_diff, p_raw, p_adj, enriched),
              names_glue = "{Comparison}__{.value}") %>%
  select(all_of(col_order))

# Enrichment summary: "Sig. [vegtype]" or "NS" per trait × comparison
dunn_wide_sig_summary <- all_dunn_results %>%
  mutate(result = ifelse(p_adj < 0.05, paste("Sig.", enriched), "NS")) %>%
  select(Trait, Comparison, result) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Comparison, values_from = result)

# Filter to traits that have at least one significant comparison
sig_traits <- all_dunn_results %>% filter(p_adj < 0.05) %>% pull(Trait) %>% unique()
dunn_wide_sig_summary_filtered <- dunn_wide_sig_summary %>% filter(Trait %in% sig_traits)

view(dunn_wide)
view(dunn_wide_sig_summary_filtered)
nrow(dunn_wide)

write.csv(dunn_wide,
          "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/NOV2024_normalized/dunn_posthoc_vegtype_GRAN3.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(dunn_wide_sig_summary_filtered,
          "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/NOV2024_normalized/dunn_enrichment_summary_GRAN3.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)

curated_bin_traits <- read.csv('/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/R_tables/curated_bin_trait_gran3.csv')
dunn_traits  <- unique(dunn_sig$Trait)
```

##### Trait category heatmap — Conifer enrichment summary
```{r trait_category_heatmap}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

# --- Load Dunn results ---
dunn_hm_raw <- read.csv(
  "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/NOV2024_normalized/dunn_posthoc_vegtype_GRAN3.csv",
  check.names = FALSE)

dunn_hm_long <- dunn_hm_raw %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Trait,
               names_to  = c("Comparison", ".value"),
               names_sep = "__") %>%
  filter(!is.na(p_adj))

# --- Filter to Conifer comparisons; flip sign so positive = Conifer enriched ---
conifer_hm <- dunn_hm_long %>%
  filter(Comparison %in% c("Aspen - Conifer", "Conifer - Meadow", "Conifer - Sagebrush")) %>%
  mutate(
    effect = if_else(Comparison == "Aspen - Conifer", -Mean_diff, Mean_diff),
    comp_label = recode(Comparison,
      "Aspen - Conifer"     = "Conifer vs Aspen",
      "Conifer - Meadow"    = "Conifer vs Meadow",
      "Conifer - Sagebrush" = "Conifer vs Sagebrush"),
    comp_label = factor(comp_label,
      levels = c("Conifer vs Meadow", "Conifer vs Sagebrush", "Conifer vs Aspen")),
    sig_label = case_when(
      p_adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_adj < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p_adj < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE          ~ "")
  )

# --- Keep only traits significant in at least one Conifer comparison ---
sig_conifer_traits <- conifer_hm %>% filter(p_adj < 0.05) %>% pull(Trait) %>% unique()
conifer_hm <- filter(conifer_hm, Trait %in% sig_conifer_traits)

# --- Category assignment (priority order; first match wins) ---
assign_cat <- function(t) {
  if (grepl("methanol\\.oxidation|methane\\.oxidation|CO2\\.fixation|formaldehyde|C1\\.compounds", t))
    return("C1 metabolism")
  # N before carbon: "anaerobic.respiration.n.denitrification" contains "aerobic" as substring
  if (grepl("ammonia\\.assimilation|ammonium\\.transport|assimilatory\\.nitrate|denitrification|aerobic\\.ammonia\\.oxidation|nitrite\\.oxidation", t))
    return("Nitrogen metabolism")
  # Carbon: aerobic respiration scoped to chemoorgano only; xyloglucan moved here from ECM
  if (grepl("chemoorganoheterotrophy\\.aerobic\\.respiration|alcohol\\.degradation|fermentation|ED\\.pathway|EMP\\.pathway|carbohydrate\\.acid\\.transport|glyoxylate|TCA\\.cycle|xyloglucan\\.breakdown", t))
    return("Carbon metabolism")
  if (grepl("amino\\.sugar\\.transport|dicarboxylate\\.transport|tricarboxylate\\.transport", t))
    return("ECM carbon substrates")
  if (grepl("N\\.compound\\.transport|urea\\.transport|amide\\.transport|nitrate\\.transport|nitrogen\\.transport|nucleoside\\.transport|nucleotide\\.transport|free\\.amino\\.acids", t))
    return("N-rich organic transport")
  if (grepl("S\\.compound\\.transport|sulfite\\.oxidation|sulfide\\.oxidation|vitamin\\.B\\.transport|siderophore\\.based\\.transport|phosphatase|phytase|organophosphorus|lipid\\.transport|carbohydrate\\.phosphate\\.transport", t))
    return("Broad nutrient scavenging")
  # Stress: carotenoids/pigments have ROS-protective roles; photosystem falls to Other
  if (grepl("ROS\\.scavenging|reactive\\.oxygen|oxidative\\.stress|redox\\.sensing|pH\\.stress|envelope\\.stress|two\\.component|osmotic\\.sens|osmolyte\\.transport|compatible\\.solute|fatty\\.acid\\.desaturase|membrane\\.stabilization|temperature.*low|low.*temperature|carotenoid|pigment", t))
    return("Stress / ROS")
  return("Other")
}

cat_levels <- c("C1 metabolism", "Carbon metabolism", "ECM carbon substrates",
                "Nitrogen metabolism", "N-rich organic transport",
                "Broad nutrient scavenging", "Stress / ROS", "Other")

conifer_hm <- conifer_hm %>%
  mutate(Category = factor(sapply(Trait, assign_cat), levels = cat_levels))

# --- Short names: strip only top-level prefix, keep the rest ---
make_short_name <- function(t) {
  t %>%
    str_remove("^Resource\\.Acquisition\\.") %>%
    str_remove("^Resource\\.Use\\.") %>%
    str_remove("^Stress\\.Tolerance\\.") %>%
    str_replace_all("\\.", " ") %>%
    str_to_sentence()
}

conifer_hm <- conifer_hm %>% mutate(short_name = make_short_name(Trait))

# --- Trait numbering: sort by category then name, assign T1..Tn ---
trait_legend <- conifer_hm %>%
  distinct(Trait, short_name, Category) %>%
  arrange(Category, short_name) %>%
  mutate(trait_num = row_number(),
         trait_label = paste0("T", trait_num))

conifer_hm <- conifer_hm %>%
  left_join(trait_legend %>% select(Trait, trait_num, trait_label), by = "Trait")

# Print legend table for reference
cat("\n--- Trait number legend ---\n")
print(trait_legend %>% select(trait_label, Category, short_name), n = Inf)

# --- Color scale: cap at 95th percentile ---
cap_val <- quantile(abs(conifer_hm$effect), 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)

fill_scale <- scale_fill_gradientn(
  colours = c("#2166AC", "#92C5DE", "#F7F7F7", "#F4A582", "#B2182B"),
  labels = function(x) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 1),
  values  = scales::rescale(c(-cap_val, -cap_val/2, 0, cap_val/2, cap_val),
                            from = c(-cap_val, cap_val)),
  limits  = c(-cap_val, cap_val),
  oob     = scales::squish,
  name    = "Mean diff\n(red = Conifer\nenriched)")

hm_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.text.y      = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, size = 7.5, face = "bold"),
        strip.background  = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = "grey70"),
        axis.text.x       = element_text(size = 8.5, angle = 25, hjust = 1),
        panel.spacing     = unit(0.3, "lines"),
        legend.position   = "right",
        legend.key.height = unit(1.5, "cm"))

# --- Split categories left/right panel ---
cats_left  <- c("C1 metabolism", "Carbon metabolism", "ECM carbon substrates", "Nitrogen metabolism")
cats_right <- c("N-rich organic transport", "Broad nutrient scavenging", "Stress / ROS", "Other")

make_panel <- function(df, cats, y_var, y_size = 6.5) {
  df_sub <- filter(df, as.character(Category) %in% cats) %>%
    mutate(Category = factor(as.character(Category), levels = cats))
  ggplot(df_sub, aes(x = comp_label,
                     y = reorder(.data[[y_var]], -as.integer(Category)),
                     fill = effect)) +
    geom_tile(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sig_label), size = 2.5, vjust = 0.8, color = "black") +
    fill_scale +
    facet_grid(Category ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y",
               labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 12)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, subtitle = "* p<0.05  ** p<0.01  *** p<0.001") +
    hm_theme +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = y_size))
}

# --- VERSION 1: full labels ---
p_left_full  <- make_panel(conifer_hm, cats_left,  "short_name")
p_right_full <- make_panel(conifer_hm, cats_right, "short_name")

library(patchwork)

# Save legend table
```

#### Differential MAG abundance on Dunn tests (April 2026)

###### Normalization of MAG meancov
```{r mag_wilcox_gran3}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# --- Output directory ---

# --- Step 1: Normalized coverage matrix (same method as microtrait pipeline) ---
# Formula: (Trimmed Mean / fastq-total) * 1e12
coverm <- read.table(
  "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Microtrait/coverm_genome/180923_coverm_output.txt",
  sep = "\t", header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE)

trimmed_cols <- grep("Trimmed Mean", colnames(coverm), value = TRUE)
meancoverage <- coverm %>% select(Genome, all_of(trimmed_cols))
colnames(meancoverage)[-1] <- sub("_trim.*", "", colnames(meancoverage)[-1])
meancoverage$Genome <- sub("\\.contigs$", "", meancoverage$Genome)

sample2bp <- read.table(
  "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Microtrait/microtrait/sample2bp.txt",
  sep = "\t", header = TRUE)
nbp <- setNames(sample2bp$fastq.total, sample2bp$sample)

meancoverage_norm <- meancoverage
for (samp in colnames(meancoverage_norm)[-1]) {
  if (samp %in% names(nbp)) {
    meancoverage_norm[[samp]] <- (meancoverage[[samp]] / nbp[samp]) * 1e12
  }
}
rownames(meancoverage_norm) <- meancoverage_norm$Genome
meancoverage_norm <- meancoverage_norm[, -1, drop = FALSE]
cov_sample_cols <- colnames(meancoverage_norm)
```

###### Runn wilcoxin on mags per dunn test comparison
```{r}
# Dunn: wide CSV -> long -> filter significant
dunn_sig <- read.csv(
  "/Users/ptasoff/My Drive/Preston_Projects/Vegtype/Analysis/Figures/sample_traits/NOV2024_normalized/dunn_posthoc_vegtype_GRAN3.csv",
  check.names = FALSE) %>%

               names_to  = c("Comparison", ".value"),
               names_sep = "__") %>%
  filter(!is.na(p_adj), p_adj < 0.05) %>%
  mutate(group1 = trimws(sub(" - .*", "", Comparison)),
         group2 = trimws(sub(".* - ", "", Comparison)))

cat("Significant Dunn rows:", nrow(dunn_sig), "\n")
cat("Significant distinct Dunn Traits:", length(unique(dunn_sig$Trait)), "\n")
nrow(dunn_sig %>% filter(enriched == "Conifer") %>% distinct(Trait))
```

```{r}
cat("Genome overlap (traits vs coverage):",
    length(intersect(curated_bin_traits$Genome, rownames(meancoverage_norm))),
    "of", nrow(curated_bin_traits), "\n")

# --- Step 3: Wilcoxon per MAG, both directions ---
run_mag_wilcox <- function(trait, group1, group2, enriched, comparison) {
  samps_g1 <- intersect(names(sample_vegtype[sample_vegtype == group1]), cov_sample_cols)
  samps_g2 <- intersect(names(sample_vegtype[sample_vegtype == group2]), cov_sample_cols)
  if (length(samps_g1) < 2 || length(samps_g2) < 2) return(NULL)

  mag_candidates <- curated_bin_traits %>%
    filter(.data[[trait]] > 0) %>%
    pull(Genome) %>%
    intersect(rownames(meancoverage_norm))
  if (length(mag_candidates) == 0) return(NULL)

  results <- lapply(mag_candidates, function(mag) {
    cov_g1 <- as.numeric(meancoverage_norm[mag, samps_g1])
    cov_g2 <- as.numeric(meancoverage_norm[mag, samps_g2])
    if (length(unique(c(cov_g1, cov_g2))) <= 1) return(NULL)
    wt <- tryCatch(wilcox.test(cov_g1, cov_g2, exact = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(wt)) return(NULL)
    m1 <- mean(cov_g1, na.rm = TRUE)
    m2 <- mean(cov_g2, na.rm = TRUE)
    data.frame(MAG = mag, mean_cov_g1 = m1, mean_cov_g2 = m2,
               log2FC   = log2((m1 + 1e-20) / (m2 + 1e-20)),
               wilcox_p = wt$p.value, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })

  res_df <- bind_rows(results)
  if (is.null(res_df) || nrow(res_df) == 0) return(NULL)

  res_df %>%
    mutate(
      wilcox_padj       = p.adjust(wilcox_p, method = "BH"),
      Trait             = trait,
      Comparison        = comparison,
      group1            = group1,
      group2            = group2,
      Enriched_vegtype  = enriched,
      direction         = ifelse(log2FC > 0, group1, group2),
      mean_cov_enriched = ifelse(enriched == group1, mean_cov_g1, mean_cov_g2),
      mean_cov_other    = ifelse(enriched == group1, mean_cov_g2, mean_cov_g1)
    )
}

all_mag_results <- pmap_df(
  list(dunn_sig$Trait, dunn_sig$group1, dunn_sig$group2,
       dunn_sig$enriched, dunn_sig$Comparison),
  run_mag_wilcox)

unique(all_mag_results$Trait) #64 traits, okay still low but...

sig_results <- all_mag_results %>%
  filter(wilcox_padj < 0.05) %>%
  left_join(taxonomy, by = c("MAG" = "Genome"))

unique(sig_results$Trait) #now only 61...why?

cat("Significant MAG rows:", nrow(sig_results), "\n")

# --- Step 4: Tables ---

# Table A: MAGs higher in enriched vegtype
table_A <- sig_results %>%
  filter(direction == Enriched_vegtype) %>%
  select(Trait, Comparison, Enriched_vegtype, MAG,
         Domain, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species,
         mean_cov_enriched, mean_cov_other, log2FC, wilcox_p, wilcox_padj) %>%
  arrange(Trait, Comparison, desc(log2FC))

# Table A2: MAGs higher in the non-enriched vegtype (losses)
table_A2 <- sig_results %>%
  filter(direction != Enriched_vegtype) %>%
  select(Trait, Comparison, Enriched_vegtype, MAG,
         Domain, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species,

# Table C: Conifer-enriched only

write.csv(table_A,  file.path(out_dir, "MAG_wilcox_enriched_GRAN3.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(table_A2, file.path(out_dir, "MAG_wilcox_other_GRAN3.csv"),    row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(table_C,  file.path(out_dir, "MAG_wilcox_conifer_GRAN3.csv"),  row.names = FALSE)

cat("Table A (enriched):", nrow(table_A),
    "| Table A2 (other):", nrow(table_A2),

# Table D: ALL MAG x trait x comparison results (sig and non-sig), taxonomy only, no HMM data
```
